A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the Event-CSL dataset and event-based sign language translation project, despite substantial methodological revision. Text, equations, tables and figures are readable throughout. Both supplied PDFs end with references and contain no appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original translation experiments on four datasets, component and sensitivity analyses, efficiency measurements and qualitative predictions in Section 5.

after.justification: V2 reports original results for EvSLT on four datasets, including new component ablations, configuration sweeps, efficiency comparisons and qualitative predictions.

M1.justification: V1 processes pooled CNN features with temporal Mamba modeling before temporal convolution and decoding. V2 introduces separate temporal and spatial branches, sequential clip-level Mamba memory aggregation, and hypergraph-guided fusion using self-attention and cross-attention. These substantially change feature processing; the gloss-free mBART decoder and cross-entropy objective remain.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Event-CSL, EvSign, PHOENIX-2014T-Event and CSL-Daily-Event, retaining the same languages, tasks and represented environments. EvCSLR is added to the contextual dataset comparison, but is not used experimentally.

E2.justification: V2 Table 2 adds SignCL and Sign2GPT and retains v1's proposed method as the Wang et al. comparator. Table 3 adds GFSLT on EvSign. The efficiency comparison replaces ResNet18, ViT and Swin variants with SignCL and Sign2GPT. Comparator membership in the two simulated-dataset translation tables remains unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 introduces temporal/spatial controls and sweeps over Mamba depth and frames per clip. It adds 112 × 112 inputs and removes the L/16 frame-sampling condition. Efficiency evaluation replaces GPU-memory reporting with FLOPs. These substantially revise the experimental design, while benchmark split sizes and BLEU/ROUGE metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V1's Mamba-removal and CNN–Mamba aggregation analyses are replaced by tests separating temporal, spatial, Mamba and graph-fusion contributions. V2 adds depth and clip-length sensitivity studies and compares graph fusion with concatenation, cross-attention and graph removal. Figure 7 adds predictions without spatial features, testing fine-detail translation rather than only comparing predictions with references.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V2's random-initialization disclosure does not establish repeated runs or uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 2–5 replace the proposed-model BLEU-4 results: Event-CSL 48.70 to 49.80, EvSign 29.41 to 20.20, PHOENIX-2014T-Event 17.53 to 16.48, and CSL-Daily-Event 8.27 to 7.09. The Event-CSL v1 result is also retained as Wang et al. These concern different models, not established matched-setting gains or losses. GFSLT's BLEU-4 changes from 17.45 to 14.72 and from 7.35 to 6.37 on the two simulated datasets without an explained setting change. Ablation, efficiency and qualitative results are also substantially revised.

T1.justification: V2 adds mathematical definitions for inter-clip memory recurrence, hypergraph incidence and normalized propagation, graph convolution, and attention-based fusion in Equations 7–11. These formalize components absent from v1. The existing SSM mathematics is largely retained or abbreviated; neither version provides theorem-based guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The methodological contribution changes from a hybrid CNN–Mamba encoder for temporal integration to EvSLT's spatial memory aggregation and graph-guided spatiotemporal interaction. The Event-CSL dataset contribution remains. V2's introduction highlights validation on two real-event datasets, although Section 5 retains experiments on all four datasets.

C2.justification: V2 develops new explanations for spatial-detail recovery, graph-mediated interaction and clip-length/depth tradeoffs. Whereas v1 reports partial benefits from increasing resolution, v2 identifies 224 × 224 as best and attributes higher-resolution degradation to noise and inadequate modeling. The limitations concerning underused high-resolution data and a small language model are retained, despite their relocation.

D1.justification: V2 specifies 200 training epochs, two randomly initialized Mamba layers, two HGCN layers, at most ten graph neighbors and eight-frame clips; it also identifies the retained dataset split as random. V1's explicit ImageNet initialization and 100-frame timing definition are no longer stated. Both retain the same code-location disclosure and future-release promise.

R1.justification: V2 reframes the research gap around neglected spatial detail and cites v1 itself as prior work. It adds EvCSLR, Sign2GPT, SignCL and several recent visual-Mamba applications, while removing discussions and citations including SignNet II, iterative prototypes and Mamba-2. GASLT is reclassified from gloss-based to gloss-free, consistent with its cited title.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, dataset descriptions and experimental discussion undergo extensive rewriting, including retained scientific content. The method narrative is reorganized around separate branches and fusion. Limitations become a standalone section, and the title and author block change.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is completely redesigned for EvSLT. The former aggregation schematic is replaced by depth/clip-length plots, and Figure 7 gains spatial-ablation comparisons. Component results receive a separate table, sensitivity tables are consolidated, and the efficiency table changes structure. Dataset examples, simulated frames and the word cloud are retained but relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the paper with additional competitive baselines, component-specific ablations and more implementation detail. However, unexplained revisions to GFSLT's simulated-dataset scores affect the claimed comparison margins. Its new efficiency comparison also omits v1's explicit timing scope and reports FLOPs without explaining how v1's stated Mamba-counting difficulty was resolved. These uncertainties concern central accuracy and efficiency evidence, so the useful additions do not establish a reliable net improvement in overall quality.
